title: Bulk load (INSERT BULK) from tedious/mssql
summary: Part of #710 (task `gaps-bulk-v1`, depends on the extension hooks in #711). - INSERT BULK table (columns) [WITH (options)] followed by a BulkLoadBCP message loads rows with SQL Server types, constraints, identity handling (KEEP_IDENTITY), CHECK_CONSTRAINTS, FIRE_TRIGGERS and KEEP_NULLS options and returns SQL Server's row count, using the existing bulk-load codec read-only. - mssql Table with request.bulk() and tedious newBulkLoad succeed for integer, string, Unicode, decimal, datetime, datetimeoffset, binary, bit and NULL values; tests assert loaded rows.

title: feat: allow to use non-default browser
summary: My default browser in Linux/KDE/Plasma is Firefox, and that's the private one I use for most everything. Alas, for AWS/day-job I use Chrome. So it'd be nice if I can tell `aws-vault` to use Chrome for `aws-vault login` and for the SSO login PKCE flow. ps. As a workaround, I currently have `AWS_VAULT_STDOUT=true` set and copy/paste the login url to Chrome manually, but obviously that is tedious.

title: Replace non-working videos with something less frustrating
summary: We know that support for videos is very limited in warc2zim (only Youtube player mostly). It would be cool to replace all video players (at least all tag) with a placeholder saying that there was a video here but it is not available in the ZIM. Ideally I would like to replace the tag by an tag, with the original video poster (not sure it is easy to grab) watermarked with something saying "video not available in ZIM". Maybe this is too much. Alternatives could be: - describe which images (based on URL regex) we want to watermark, with which text (and keep the video player as-is) => this is going to be a bit frustrating for the user because he can still start the video but at least this ensure we can easily cover all kind of video players - instead of replacing with an image of the original video poster, just replace with a text saying there was a video which is not available in the ZIM (but then we need to be able to localize this message in proper languages).
